subject: Renewal procurement: SOC 2 Type II report, bridge letter, and audit-window clarification
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@lanewayhealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@lanewayhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: LaneWay renewal — SOC 2 Type II + bridge and audit window questions

Hi Olga,

We're kicking off LaneWay's renewal procurement for the next contract year and procurement needs the following to complete our security review and SOW routing:

- Latest SOC 2 Type II report (covering at least through Dec 31, 2026)
- If the Type II period does not cover our renewal window, a bridge letter confirming coverage and the exact audit window and any mitigating controls
- Confirmation whether Redwood will provide a signed bridge letter on company letterhead or whether we should accept a signed attestation PDF
- A rough delivery date for the items above (we're targeting completion by 3/22)

Also: LaneWay uses a condensed SIG questionnaire for platform vendors. Can you confirm whether you can provide either full SIG responses or the CAIQ equivalent? If full SIG will take longer, a prioritized subset that maps to data residency, encryption (in transit + at rest), and access controls would suffice.

Thanks — can you loop in whoever owns compliance artifacts?

Jordan

Subject: Re: LaneWay renewal — SOC 2 Type II + bridge and audit window questions

Hi Jordan — thanks for the clear list. We're on it. Quick answers up front:

- We can provide the SOC 2 Type II report covering the period Jan 1, 2026 — Dec 31, 2026 as a PDF. Final copy is attached.
- If you need a formal bridge letter, we will provide a signed bridge letter on Redwood Inference letterhead that states the audit window and whether controls materially changed since the report period. Marcus has the bridge template and will propose language for your review.
- Target delivery for the signed bridge letter: by 3/19 EOD (we can expedite if you need earlier).
- SIG/CAIQ: we maintain a CAIQ mapping and can export prioritized SIG sections. We'll attach a prioritized spreadsheet (data residency, encryption, access controls) this afternoon and follow up with the full SIG export if required.

Marcus/Rishi — can you: (1) attach the finalized SOC 2 PDF (we have a secured copy), (2) drop a draft bridge letter (DOCX) in this thread, and (3) confirm whether any control changes occurred that should appear in the bridge? LaneWay prefers a signed PDF; please note.

Jordan — once we send the draft bridge letter, feel free to request edits. If procurement needs DocuSign, we can route it that way.

Best,

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Draft bridge letter + SIG extract (prioritized)

Hi all — attaching a first draft of the bridge letter and a prioritized SIG extract (spreadsheet) that maps to LaneWay's asks. Key points in the bridge:

- Audit period stated: Jan 1, 2026 — Dec 31, 2026.
- Control statement: "No material changes to controls that would affect the trust services criteria were identified since the report date." (we can swap wording if legal wants a different formulation).
- Intended signatures: Director, Compliance & Head of Security (we will sign on Redwood letterhead and provide a PDF).

Notes on SIG/CAIQ: the prioritized extract covers data residency, encryption (TLS 1.2+ in transit, AES-256 at rest), key management integrations (KMS/HSM options), and role-based access control. Full SIG export will follow by 3/18.

Jordan — can you confirm whether LaneWay requires the bridge to be notarized or if a signed PDF is sufficient for procurement? Also confirming: you asked for delivery by 3/22; we plan to deliver signed bridge + prioritized SIG by 3/19 (as Olga said).

Marcus Lin
Sr. Compliance Manager | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

Attachments: SOC2-Bridge-Letter-Draft.docx; SIG-Partial-Responses.xlsx

Thanks Marcus/Olga — this is perfect. A few quick clarifications so procurement can close the packet today:

1) Signed PDF of the bridge letter is acceptable; no notarization needed. DocuSign is preferred.
2) Please include a one-paragraph plain-language summary in the bridge letter highlighting whether any control exceptions were open at report issuance and whether those were remediated.
3) Can you drop the final signed bridge (DocuSign) and the prioritized SIG spreadsheet in our Drive folder by 3/19 5pm PT? Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/laneway-redwood-renewal-2027

If you hit any snags, call me directly. Otherwise we'll proceed to routing.

—Jordan
